$libraryComment: The colour library: seventeen hue ramps shipped beside the semantic ones,
for consumers to build with (--primitiv-color-violet-500 and so on).
Derived, not picked. The five `sameAs` hues ARE the semantic ramps -- red is
generated from danger's seed -- so the token layer never carries two
almost-identical reds. They keep their own values rather than aliasing, so a
project that re-seeds `danger` with `primitiv theme` does not turn red orange.
The other twelve sit evenly between those five anchor hues on the OkLCH
wheel. Each one's lightness, and its chroma as a share of what sRGB allows
at that lightness and hue, are interpolated from its two neighbouring
anchors. The seeds below are the result, written to five places of OkLCH.
Two exceptions, by design choice: yellow and lime keep their derived hue
but sit at a higher lightness (0.84 and 0.80), with chroma at 92% of the
sRGB limit there. Derived strictly they came out mustard and olive at 500;
a yellow only reads as yellow when it is light. 0.84 is the brightest
yellow that keeps comfortable step spacing in both themes.
Guarded by crates/harmoni-core/tests/colour_library.rs, and covered by the
same ramp-quality gates as the semantic ramps (tests/ramp_regression.rs).
